transcript: This is Acropulse Open Mike. I'm your host, Jeff Natalie. Our guest this week is Iowa U.S. Senator Joni Ernst. Acropulse Open Mike is brought to you by the American Sugar Alliance. Learn more about the benefits of the sugar industry to the nation at sugaralliance.org. Acropulse Open Mike continues with Senator Joni Ernst. Next. America's 11,000 sugar-buted sugar cane farmers produce sugar under some of the world's strictest safety, labor, and environmental standards. The industry also supports 151,000 jobs across more than two dozen states. The farmer, family, and employee-owned sugar companies pay workers fair wages and offer good benefits, including union jobs and rural and urban communities. Together, farmers and workers provide a reliable domestic sugar supply chain for both food manufacturers and grocery store shoppers. A strong bipartisan coalition in Congress supports sugar policy, which is the safety net for sugar producers in the Farm Bill. The sugar program is designed to have zero cost to the taxpayer and has the flexibility to allow for a reliable supply of sugar throughout the year. Sugar policy ensures Americans are not dependent on unreliable foreign supplies which would displace American farmers and jobs and jeopardize domestic food security for this essential ingredient. For more, visit the American Sugar Alliance at sugaralliance.org. This is Agropulse Open Mike. The U.S. Congress was successful in avoiding a government shutdown last week, but so far, fallen short of approving a new farm bill. Iowa Senator Joni Ernst helps for better chances in 2025. On trade, Ernst is very displeased with the growing U.S. Ag trade deficit and says the Biden administration isn't making trade a priority.
